DPS.name: Bali
DPS.description: Bali is a living postcard — volcanic mountains, ancient temples, lush rice terraces, and world-class surf breaks. Whether you seek spiritual retreat, adventure, or pure indulgence, Bali delivers.
DPS.visaRequirements: Indians require a visa on arrival (USD 35, valid 30 days)

highlights.name: Tanah Lot Temple
highlights.description: A 16th-century sea temple perched on a rocky outcrop, most magical at sunset.

highlights.name: Ubud Monkey Forest
highlights.description: A sacred forest sanctuary housing 749 long-tailed macaques among ancient temples and towering trees.

highlights.name: Tegallalang Rice Terraces
highlights.description: Iconic UNESCO-listed rice paddies carved into the hillside near Ubud. The subak irrigation system here dates back to the 9th century.

highlights.name: Seminyak Beach
highlights.description: Bali's most sophisticated beach strip — premium beach clubs, world-class sunsets, and celebrity chef restaurants.

highlights.name: Uluwatu Kecak Fire Dance
highlights.description: Watch the dramatic Kecak dance performed at cliff-edge Uluwatu Temple as the sun sets over the Indian Ocean.

neighborhoods.name: Seminyak
neighborhoods.vibe: Upscale beach clubs, boutiques, fine dining

neighborhoods.name: Ubud
neighborhoods.vibe: Arts, spirituality, jungle, wellness retreats

neighborhoods.name: Nusa Dua
neighborhoods.vibe: Luxury resorts, private beaches, water sports

neighborhoods.name: Canggu
neighborhoods.vibe: Surfer culture, digital nomads, cafes, nightlife

neighborhoods.name: Kuta
neighborhoods.vibe: Budget-friendly, busy nightlife, shopping

tips: Rent a scooter — it's the best way to explore at your own pace (₹400–600/day).
Dress modestly when visiting temples — a sarong is required (usually provided).
Eat at warungs (local family restaurants) for the best nasi goreng at a fraction of hotel prices.
Book popular spots like Potato Head or Ku De Ta beach clubs in advance.
The Gili Islands are a 2-hour fast-boat ride — add them to a longer itinerary.

SYD.name: Sydney
SYD.description: Sydney is Australia's dazzling gateway — a city of iconic landmarks, pristine beaches, world-class cuisine, and an outdoor lifestyle that's impossible to resist. It's equally spectacular for business and leisure.
SYD.bestTimeToVisit: September to November and March to May (shoulder seasons)
SYD.visaRequirements: Indians require a visitor visa (apply online via ImmiAccount, typically 2–4 weeks)

highlights.name: Sydney Opera House
highlights.description: One of the 20th century's greatest architectural achievements. Catch a performance, take a backstage tour, or simply admire it from the ferry.

highlights.name: Bondi Beach
highlights.description: Australia's most famous beach — great surf, the Bondi to Coogee coastal walk, and the Icebergs ocean pool.

highlights.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge Climb
highlights.description: Climb to the summit of the Harbour Bridge for 360° views of Sydney. One of the world's most thrilling urban experiences.
highlights.bestTime: Twilight climb for golden hour views

highlights.name: Blue Mountains
highlights.description: A UNESCO World Heritage wilderness 90 minutes from Sydney. See the Three Sisters, Wentworth Falls, and vast eucalyptus forests.

highlights.name: The Rocks Markets
highlights.description: Sydney's oldest neighbourhood hosts weekend markets with artisans, food stalls, and live music under the shadow of the Harbour Bridge.

neighborhoods.name: CBD & Circular Quay
neighborhoods.vibe: Business hub, Opera House, ferries, fine dining

neighborhoods.name: The Rocks
neighborhoods.vibe: Heritage sandstone, boutique hotels, weekend markets

neighborhoods.name: Surry Hills
neighborhoods.vibe: Cafes, galleries, independent restaurants, craft beer

neighborhoods.name: Darling Harbour
neighborhoods.vibe: Tourism precinct, aquarium, museums, restaurants

neighborhoods.name: Newtown
neighborhoods.vibe: Eclectic, diverse, vintage shopping, live music

tips: Get an Opal card for seamless public transport (train, bus, ferry, light rail).
The ferry to Manly is one of the world's great commutes — do it at least once.
Book Bondi Icebergs pool entry online to avoid queues.
Sydney restaurants are exceptional but expensive — allow AUD 80–120 per head for a quality dinner.
If combining with Melbourne, the XPT overnight train is a scenic alternative to flying.

LHR.name: London
LHR.description: London is a city that defies superlatives — 2,000 years of history layered with world-leading museums, theatre, fashion, finance, and food from every corner of the globe. Business or pleasure, London always delivers.
LHR.bestTimeToVisit: June to August (warm and long days), December (Christmas markets)
LHR.visaRequirements: Indians require a Standard Visitor Visa (apply online, typically 3 weeks)

highlights.name: The British Museum
highlights.description: Home to 8 million works spanning human history from the Rosetta Stone to the Elgin Marbles. One of the world's greatest free museums.

highlights.name: Tower of London
highlights.description: A 1,000-year-old castle housing the Crown Jewels, Beefeater Yeoman guards, and the legendary ravens.

highlights.name: West End Theatre
highlights.description: The world's greatest concentration of theatre. From Les Misérables to Hamilton to new productions — always something unmissable.

highlights.name: Borough Market
highlights.description: London's oldest and most celebrated food market — artisan cheeses, charcuterie, street food from 50 countries, and exceptional coffee.

highlights.name: Hyde Park
highlights.description: 350 acres in the heart of London — the Serpentine lake, outdoor concerts, Speaker's Corner, and the Diana Memorial.

neighborhoods.name: Mayfair & St James's
neighborhoods.vibe: Luxury hotels, fine dining, private members clubs

neighborhoods.name: Covent Garden
neighborhoods.vibe: Theatre, opera, market, street performers

neighborhoods.name: Shoreditch
neighborhoods.vibe: Tech startups, street art, nightlife, brunch

neighborhoods.name: South Kensington
neighborhoods.vibe: Museums, embassies, affordable cafes

neighborhoods.name: Canary Wharf
neighborhoods.vibe: Financial district, excellent transport links

tips: Get an Oyster card or use contactless payment on the Tube — it's always cheaper than paper tickets.
Most major museums and galleries are free — plan your free days strategically.
Book theatre tickets on TodayTix or at the TKTS booth in Leicester Square for discounts.
London weather is famously unpredictable — always carry a light layer.
The Elizabeth line (Crossrail) connects Heathrow to central London in ~30 minutes.

DXB.name: Dubai
DXB.tagline: Where the Future Meets the Desert
DXB.description: Dubai is the world's most audacious city — record-breaking skyscrapers, man-made islands, indoor ski slopes in the desert, and more Michelin stars than many European capitals. Increasingly popular for business events, incentive travel, and luxury shopping.
DXB.visaRequirements: Indians receive a visa on arrival (free, valid 14 days with return ticket)

highlights.name: Burj Khalifa
highlights.description: The world's tallest building at 828m. The At The Top observation deck on the 148th floor offers staggering views across the Gulf.

highlights.name: Dubai Mall & Dubai Fountain
highlights.description: The world's largest shopping mall — with an Olympic-size ice rink, indoor aquarium, and a 30-acre outdoor fountain show every evening.

highlights.name: Dubai Desert Safari
highlights.description: A quintessential Dubai experience — dune bashing in a 4x4, camel riding, sandboarding, and a Bedouin camp dinner under the stars.

highlights.name: Dubai Creek & Old Souk
highlights.description: The historic heart of Dubai — take an abra (wooden water taxi) across the creek and explore the Gold Souk and Spice Souk.

highlights.name: Palm Jumeirah
highlights.description: The world's largest man-made island, home to Atlantis, the Palm Monorail, and the best beach clubs in Dubai.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown Dubai
neighborhoods.vibe: Burj Khalifa, Dubai Mall, premium hotels

neighborhoods.name: Jumeirah Beach Residence (JBR)
neighborhoods.vibe: Beach promenade, outdoor dining, The Walk

neighborhoods.name: DIFC
neighborhoods.vibe: Financial centre, art galleries, upscale restaurants

neighborhoods.name: Deira / Old Dubai
neighborhoods.vibe: Souks, heritage, local food, budget accommodation

neighborhoods.name: Business Bay
neighborhoods.vibe: New CBD, canal views, business hotels

tips: Dress modestly in public areas (not beach/hotel) — shoulders and knees covered.
Ramadan changes operating hours significantly — restaurants close during daylight hours.
The Dubai Metro is excellent — covers most tourist areas and costs almost nothing.
Duty-free shopping at Dubai Airport is genuinely excellent — especially for perfumes and electronics.
Taxi and Uber are affordable — most rides within the city are under ₹800.

SIN.name: Singapore
SIN.description: Singapore punches far above its weight — a tiny city-state that leads the world in aviation, finance, food, and urban planning. Immaculately clean, hyper-efficient, and endlessly surprising. An ideal stopover or standalone destination.
SIN.visaRequirements: Indians can obtain a 96-hour transit visa-free; for longer stays, apply for a short-term visit pass (free, processed on arrival for eligible travelers)

highlights.name: Gardens by the Bay
highlights.description: A futuristic park of supertrees, climate-controlled biomes (the Flower Dome and Cloud Forest), and spectacular nightly light shows.
highlights.bestTime: Evening for the Spectra light show

highlights.name: Hawker Centres
highlights.description: Singapore's UNESCO-listed hawker culture — hundreds of food stalls at Maxwell, Lau Pa Sat, and Old Airport Road serving incredible food for under SGD 10.

highlights.name: Sentosa Island
highlights.description: Singapore's resort island — Universal Studios, S.E.A. Aquarium, beach clubs, and Singapore Cable Car rides.

highlights.name: Chinatown & Little India
highlights.description: Two of Singapore's most vibrant heritage districts — temples, street food, spice shops, and beautifully preserved shophouses.
highlights.bestTime: Morning for temples, evening for food

highlights.name: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark
highlights.description: The 200m-high infinity pool and observation deck connecting Singapore's most iconic three towers. Views are breathtaking day and night.

neighborhoods.name: Marina Bay
neighborhoods.vibe: Iconic skyline, MBS, Gardens by the Bay

neighborhoods.name: Orchard Road
neighborhoods.vibe: Shopping megamall strip, luxury brands

neighborhoods.name: Kampong Glam
neighborhoods.vibe: Malay heritage, street art, indie cafes

neighborhoods.name: Clarke Quay / Robertson Quay
neighborhoods.vibe: Nightlife, restaurants, riverside bars

neighborhoods.name: Tiong Bahru
neighborhoods.vibe: Hipster cafes, bookshops, art deco architecture

tips: Chewing gum is prohibited to import and sell — don't try to smuggle any.
The MRT (metro) covers the entire island efficiently — EZ-Link card is a must.
Eating at hawker centres is a cultural experience, not just a budget option — Michelin-starred stalls cost SGD 3.
Singapore is extremely walkable between attractions in cooler evening hours.
Changi Airport is world-class — arrive early and explore the Jewel waterfall complex.

BKK.name: Bangkok
BKK.description: Bangkok is a city of extremes — ancient temples beside futuristic malls, Michelin-starred restaurants next to street stalls, chaotic traffic and serene waterways. It's one of the world's great cities and an endlessly compelling travel destination.
BKK.bestTimeToVisit: November to February (cool and dry season)
BKK.visaRequirements: Indians can enter visa-free for 30 days (as of 2024)

highlights.name: Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha)
highlights.description: Thailand's most sacred temple within the Grand Palace complex. Home to the 14th-century Emerald Buddha, carved from a single block of jade.

highlights.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
highlights.description: One of the world's largest markets — over 15,000 stalls selling everything from street food to vintage clothing, antiques, and live plants.

highlights.name: Chao Phraya River Cruise
highlights.description: The Chao Phraya is Bangkok's main artery — a dinner cruise or public ferry ride passes temples, palaces, and a side of the city invisible from land.

highlights.name: Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn)
highlights.description: A stunning 87m tower encrusted with colorful porcelain fragments on the west bank of the Chao Phraya. Especially photogenic at sunrise and dusk.

highlights.name: Khao San Road
highlights.description: The world-famous backpacker street — street food, rooftop bars, live music, and the cheapest cocktails you'll find anywhere in Asia.

neighborhoods.name: Sukhumvit
neighborhoods.vibe: Expats, nightlife, BTS access, malls

neighborhoods.name: Silom / Sathorn
neighborhoods.vibe: Finance district, rooftop bars, LGBTQ+ friendly

neighborhoods.name: Banglamphu / Khao San Rd
neighborhoods.vibe: Budget travel, temples, backpacker scene

neighborhoods.name: Ari / Phrom Phong
neighborhoods.vibe: Cafes, local eateries, quieter residential

neighborhoods.name: Chinatown (Yaowarat)
neighborhoods.vibe: Street food, gold shops, night markets

tips: Never point your feet at a Buddha image or at a Thai person — it's considered disrespectful.
The BTS Skytrain and MRT metro avoid Bangkok's notorious traffic — use them for daytime travel.
Eat pad thai and mango sticky rice from street stalls, not restaurants — the stalls are better.
Thailand has strict laws on insulting the monarchy — avoid any commentary.
The Grab app is the easiest way to get metered fares — better than negotiating with tuk-tuks.

NRT.name: Tokyo
NRT.description: Tokyo is the world's most populous metropolis and arguably its most captivating — a seamless blend of ancient shrines and neon-lit skyscrapers, Michelin-starred ramen stalls and century-old tea houses. Perfectly safe, immaculately clean, and endlessly fascinating.
NRT.bestTimeToVisit: March to May (cherry blossom) and October to November (autumn foliage)
NRT.visaRequirements: Indians require a Japan tourist visa (apply at Japanese consulate, typically 5–7 working days; free of charge)

highlights.name: Senso-ji Temple, Asakusa
highlights.description: Tokyo's oldest and most beloved temple, dating to 645 AD. The iconic Kaminarimon gate, Nakamise shopping street, and the five-storey pagoda are unmissable.

highlights.name: Shibuya Crossing
highlights.description: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing — up to 3,000 people cross simultaneously when the lights change. Best viewed from the Starbucks or Mag's Park overlooking the scramble.

highlights.name: teamLab Borderless / Planets
highlights.description: A revolutionary digital art museum where immersive light installations dissolve the boundary between art and viewer. One of Tokyo's most photographed modern attractions.

highlights.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
highlights.description: Tokyo's legendary fish market precinct — tuna sashimi at 6 AM, fresh tamago tamagoyaki, and the freshest seafood breakfast you'll ever eat.

highlights.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
highlights.description: A 58-hectare oasis in the heart of Tokyo combining French formal, English landscape, and traditional Japanese garden styles. Peak cherry blossom in late March.
highlights.bestTime: Late March to early April (cherry blossom)

neighborhoods.name: Shinjuku
neighborhoods.vibe: Entertainment, nightlife, Kabukicho, Golden Gai bars

neighborhoods.name: Shibuya
neighborhoods.vibe: Youth fashion, iconic crossing, department stores

neighborhoods.name: Asakusa
neighborhoods.vibe: Traditional Tokyo, temples, rickshaws, street food

neighborhoods.name: Ginza
neighborhoods.vibe: Luxury shopping, galleries, high-end dining

neighborhoods.name: Harajuku / Omotesando
neighborhoods.vibe: Street fashion, boutiques, crepe stalls, cafes

tips: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport — it works on all trains, buses, and at convenience stores.
Japan is still very cash-oriented — carry JPY, especially in smaller restaurants and shrines.
Buy a pocket Wi-Fi or SIM at the airport; Google Maps + translate are essential.
Shoes that slip on and off easily are a must — you'll remove them constantly at temples, ryokans, and many restaurants.
7-Eleven, FamilyMart, and Lawson convenience stores serve genuinely excellent, cheap food — don't overlook them.

CDG.name: Paris
CDG.description: Paris is the undisputed capital of romance, art, and gastronomy. From the Eiffel Tower to the Louvre, from Montmartre's cobblestoned lanes to the grand boulevards of Haussmann, every arrondissement rewards exploration. The world's most visited city for good reason.
CDG.bestTimeToVisit: April to June and September to October (mild weather, fewer crowds)
CDG.visaRequirements: Indians require a Schengen visa (apply at French consulate/VFS, typically 15 days processing; covers all Schengen countries)

highlights.name: Eiffel Tower
highlights.description: Gustave Eiffel's 1889 iron masterpiece — the world's most visited paid monument. Take the lift to the summit (276m) for panoramic views across Paris.
highlights.bestTime: Sunset and after dark (hourly light show)

highlights.name: The Louvre Museum
highlights.description: The world's largest art museum and home to the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and 35,000 other works. Allow a full day — you can't see everything in one visit.
highlights.bestTime: Wednesday/Friday evenings (open until 9:45 PM, less crowded)

highlights.name: Montmartre & Sacré-Cœur
highlights.description: Paris's bohemian hilltop village — artists, cabarets, the white-domed Sacré-Cœur basilica, and the best view over the city's rooftops.

highlights.name: Musée d'Orsay
highlights.description: Housed in a stunning Beaux-Arts railway station, the Orsay holds the world's greatest collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist art — Monet, Renoir, Van Gogh, Degas.

highlights.name: Seine River Cruise
highlights.description: A Bateaux Mouches or Vedettes du Pont Neuf cruise passes every major Paris monument from the water. Magical at dusk and after dark.

neighborhoods.name: Le Marais (3rd & 4th)
neighborhoods.vibe: Historic mansions, Jewish quarter, boutiques, LGBTQ+ hub

neighborhoods.name: Saint-Germain-des-Prés (6th)
neighborhoods.vibe: Literary cafes, galleries, fashion, intellectual Paris

neighborhoods.name: Montmartre (18th)
neighborhoods.vibe: Artists, Sacré-Cœur, vintage shops, local bistros

neighborhoods.name: Champs-Élysées / 8th
neighborhoods.vibe: Luxury brands, Arc de Triomphe, grand hotels

neighborhoods.name: Bastille / 11th
neighborhoods.vibe: Nightlife, craft beer bars, markets, young Parisians

tips: The Paris Metro is excellent — buy a carnet of 10 tickets or a weekly Navigo pass for best value.
Most world-class museums are free on the first Sunday of each month — plan around this.
Book Eiffel Tower tickets weeks in advance online — queue on the day can be 3+ hours.
Parisians appreciate even a basic 'Bonjour' and 'Merci' — always greet shop staff.
Boulangeries sell the best and cheapest breakfast in Paris — croissant and café au lait for under ₹400.

JFK.name: New York
JFK.description: New York City is the world's most iconic urban destination — a vertical metropolis of 8 million stories, where Wall Street meets Broadway, Central Park borders skyscrapers, and the best food from every country on earth is within a subway ride. Exhausting, exhilarating, and utterly unforgettable.
JFK.bestTimeToVisit: April to June and September to November (comfortable temperatures)
JFK.visaRequirements: Indians require a B1/B2 visitor visa (apply at US consulate/VFS; interview required; allow 4–8 weeks)

highlights.name: Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island
highlights.description: The enduring symbol of American freedom — take the ferry from Battery Park to Liberty Island and explore the Ellis Island Immigration Museum.
highlights.bestTime: First morning ferry (9 AM) to avoid crowds

highlights.name: Central Park
highlights.description: 843 acres of green space in the heart of Manhattan — Bethesda Fountain, Strawberry Fields, the Reservoir, the Zoo, and the Great Lawn.

highlights.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art (The Met)
highlights.description: One of the world's greatest art museums — spanning 5,000 years of human creativity from Egyptian mummies to Picasso. The rooftop garden bar is a highlight.

highlights.name: Times Square
highlights.description: The world's most famous intersection — neon billboards, Broadway theatres, the New Year's Eve ball drop, and the electric pulse of midtown Manhattan.

highlights.name: High Line & Chelsea Market
highlights.description: A 2.3km elevated park built on a disused rail line. Below it, Chelsea Market's gourmet food hall is the best lunch spot in Manhattan.

neighborhoods.name: Midtown Manhattan
neighborhoods.vibe: Empire State, Times Square, Fifth Avenue shopping

neighborhoods.name: Lower East Side / SoHo
neighborhoods.vibe: Galleries, indie boutiques, brunch culture, trendy bars

neighborhoods.name: Brooklyn (Williamsburg)
neighborhoods.vibe: Hipster scene, skyline views, craft breweries, street art

neighborhoods.name: Upper West Side
neighborhoods.vibe: Central Park access, residential calm, museum mile

neighborhoods.name: Financial District
neighborhoods.vibe: Wall Street, 9/11 Memorial, ferry terminals, history

tips: Get a MetroCard or tap your contactless card on the subway — it runs 24/7 and costs USD 2.90 per ride.
Tipping is not optional in the US — 18–22% at restaurants, USD 1–2 per drink at bars.
Book Broadway shows in advance via TodayTix or TKTS booth for same-day discounts up to 50%.
The free Staten Island Ferry gives stunning Statue of Liberty views — no ticket needed.
NYC Bagels and dollar pizza slices are cultural institutions — seek them out.

MLE.name: Maldives
MLE.description: The Maldives is 1,200 coral islands strung across the Indian Ocean — turquoise lagoons, powder-white beaches, and overwater bungalows hovering above some of the world's clearest water. The world's lowest country (average 1.5m above sea level) is also its most dreamlike.
MLE.bestTimeToVisit: November to April (dry northeast monsoon season)
MLE.currency: Maldivian Rufiyaa (MVR) — US dollars widely accepted
MLE.visaRequirements: Indians receive a free 30-day on-arrival visa (no prior application needed)

highlights.name: Overwater Bungalow Stay
highlights.description: The quintessential Maldives experience — a thatched villa on stilts above the lagoon, with a glass floor panel revealing the reef below and a private ladder into the sea.
highlights.bestTime: Any time (sunrises and sunsets are equally spectacular)

highlights.name: Snorkelling & Diving
highlights.description: The Maldives sits on the world's 7th largest barrier reef system. Encounter manta rays, whale sharks, sea turtles, and kaleidoscopic coral gardens — often just metres from shore.

highlights.name: Biyadhoo Island House Reef
highlights.description: One of the Maldives' most accessible house reefs — a coral wall dropping to 30m with frequent reef shark sightings and massive schools of tropical fish.

highlights.name: Malé City & Friday Mosque
highlights.description: The world's most densely populated capital — the 17th-century Friday Mosque (Hukuru Miskiy) is the oldest in the Maldives, built from coral stone.

highlights.name: Sandbank Picnic
highlights.description: A private sandbank — a strip of white sand barely above the waterline surrounded by infinite blue — is the most romantic lunch venue on the planet.

neighborhoods.name: North Malé Atoll
neighborhoods.vibe: Most resorts, closest to airport, easy transfers

neighborhoods.name: South Malé Atoll
neighborhoods.vibe: More remote resorts, great dive sites

neighborhoods.name: Ari Atoll
neighborhoods.vibe: Whale shark hotspot, luxury resorts, longer transfers

neighborhoods.name: Malé City
neighborhoods.vibe: Capital, local guesthouses, budget-friendly, authentic

tips: Speedboat transfers from Malé airport are 20–45 minutes; seaplane transfers cost USD 300–600 round-trip but are spectacular.
All-inclusive packages at Maldives resorts are worth the premium — food and drinks on islands are very expensive.
Bring reef-safe sunscreen — chemical sunscreens are banned to protect the coral.
Many islands are uninhabited — resorts often have exclusive use of their island, which is part of the appeal.
Alcohol is only available at resort islands, not on local islands or in Malé.

KUL.name: Kuala Lumpur
KUL.description: Kuala Lumpur is Southeast Asia's most underrated city — a thrilling mix of Malay, Chinese, and Indian cultures set against the backdrop of the iconic Petronas Twin Towers. Exceptional food, excellent shopping, and a cost of living that makes it one of the world's great value destinations.
KUL.bestTimeToVisit: May to July and December to February (drier periods)
KUL.visaRequirements: Indians can apply for a Malaysia eNTRI (₹900 approx, single entry, 15 days) or eVISA online; also eligible for 30-day eVISA on arrival at select airports

highlights.name: Petronas Twin Towers
highlights.description: The world's tallest twin towers at 452m, connected by a sky bridge on the 41st floor. The KLCC park fountain show at night is one of KL's finest free spectacles.

highlights.name: Batu Caves
highlights.description: A Hindu temple complex inside a limestone hill, reached by 272 colourful steps past the 42.7m golden Lord Murugan statue — one of the tallest statues in the world.

highlights.name: Jalan Alor Night Market
highlights.description: KL's most famous food street — grilled satay, char kway teow, durian, and hundreds of street food stalls packed into one electrifying lantern-lit lane.

highlights.name: Bukit Bintang Shopping Belt
highlights.description: KL's Golden Triangle — Pavilion KL, Starhill Gallery, Fahrenheit88, and Low Yat Plaza for electronics. Some of Asia's best mall shopping at fraction of Singapore prices.

highlights.name: KL Forest Eco Park
highlights.description: A virgin rainforest canopy walkway in the city centre, steps from the Petronas Towers. A rare chance to walk among 130-million-year-old trees inside a major metropolis.

neighborhoods.name: Bukit Bintang / KLCC
neighborhoods.vibe: Shopping, nightlife, Petronas Towers, luxury hotels

neighborhoods.name: Chow Kit / Little India
neighborhoods.vibe: Authentic local markets, spices, textiles, street food

neighborhoods.name: Bangsar
neighborhoods.vibe: Expat cafes, weekend brunch, independent boutiques

neighborhoods.name: Brickfields (Little India)
neighborhoods.vibe: South Indian food, temples, fabric shops

neighborhoods.name: Chinatown (Petaling Street)
neighborhoods.vibe: Night market, dim sum, heritage shophouses

tips: Grab (the regional Uber) is essential in KL — taxis rarely use meters and Grab is far cheaper.
The MRT, LRT, and monorail lines cover most tourist areas — a Touch 'n Go card works across all transit.
KL is an outstanding food city — nasi lemak, roti canai, and laksa are best at local mamak stalls.
The KLIA Ekspres train from KL Sentral to the airport takes 28 minutes — far faster than any taxi.
Dress modestly when visiting mosques — a headscarf and covered shoulders/knees are required for women.

HKG.name: Hong Kong
HKG.description: Hong Kong is a spectacular collision of East and West — British colonial heritage and Chinese culture layered over one of the world's most dramatic harbours. A city of superlatives: the world's most vertical cityscape, extraordinary Cantonese cuisine, and a shopping and dining scene without equal in Asia.
HKG.bestTimeToVisit: October to December (cool, low humidity, clear skies)
HKG.visaRequirements: Indians require a Hong Kong visa (apply online via Immigration Dept; typically 4–6 weeks; separate from China mainland visa)

highlights.name: Victoria Peak & The Peak Tram
highlights.description: Hong Kong's most iconic view — take the historic funicular tram to Victoria Peak for a 360-degree panorama of the harbour, Kowloon, and the South China Sea.

highlights.name: Symphony of Lights
highlights.description: The world's largest permanent light and sound show — 44 buildings on both sides of Victoria Harbour synchronise lights and lasers nightly at 8 PM.
highlights.entryFee: Free (best viewed from Tsim Sha Tsui waterfront)

highlights.name: Temple Street Night Market
highlights.description: Kowloon's legendary night market — fortune tellers, Cantonese opera performers, street food, and stalls selling everything from jade to fake designer goods.

highlights.name: Dim Sum at a Traditional Teahouse
highlights.description: Yum cha (drinking tea with dim sum) is a Hong Kong institution. Lin Heung Kui, Tim Ho Wan, and Lung King Heen represent the full range from traditional to Michelin-starred.

highlights.name: Big Buddha & Po Lin Monastery, Lantau
highlights.description: A 34m bronze Buddha atop Ngong Ping Plateau on Lantau Island, reached by the spectacular Ngong Ping 360 cable car. One of the world's largest outdoor seated Buddhas.

neighborhoods.name: Central & Admiralty
neighborhoods.vibe: Finance, luxury hotels, world-class restaurants, IFC mall

neighborhoods.name: Causeway Bay
neighborhoods.vibe: Shopping, Times Square mall, restaurants, nightlife

neighborhoods.name: Tsim Sha Tsui (TST)
neighborhoods.vibe: Harbour views, museums, night market, budget hotels

neighborhoods.name: Sheung Wan / Sai Ying Pun
neighborhoods.vibe: Art galleries, antiques, indie cafes, PMQ

neighborhoods.name: Mong Kok
neighborhoods.vibe: Bustling street markets, electronics, local food

tips: Get an Octopus card at the airport — it works on all MTR, buses, ferries, trams, and at 7-Elevens.
The Star Ferry between Central and Tsim Sha Tsui costs HKD 2.70 — the cheapest harbour view in the world.
Hong Kong's wet markets are a cultural experience — Wet Market in Sai Ying Pun is especially authentic.
The MTR is impeccably clean, punctual, and air-conditioned — use it as your primary transport.
Book the Michelin-starred Tim Ho Wan weeks in advance — it's the world's most affordable Michelin restaurant.
